# Florence 1347 – Communication & information

- **Writing (signs that record language)** [`writing_invention`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/writing_invention.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high
- **Alphabet and mass literacy** [`alphabet_writing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/alphabet_writing.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Florence is unusually literate: Villani counts 8,000–10,000 children learning to read (c. 1338). Merchants and artisans write Tuscan in merchant script. Peasants and most women do not. Local: reading masters; Giovanni Villani's figures.
- **Codex book and finding aids** [`codex_book`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/codex_book.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Every book is copied by hand on parchment or paper. Leaf numbers and tables of chapters are rare; friars have concordances and alphabetical indexes. A book costs months of wages. Local: cartolai (stationers) near the Badia; convent scriptoria; paper from Fabriano. Elsewhere: Bologna and Paris, university stationers renting out quires (pecia).
- **Woodblock printing** [`woodblock_printing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/woodblock_printing.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept high. Seals and coin dies are familiar; some cloth is stamped with carved blocks. Nobody prints images or text on paper, though woodcarvers, paper and lampblack ink are all here. Local: woodcarvers and painters' workshops; cartolai. Elsewhere: China and Korea, books printed from woodblocks for centuries; Egypt, block-printed amulets.
- **Movable-type printing press** [`printing_press`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/printing_press.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept high. No printing exists in Europe. Knowledge spreads by sermon, council decree, notary and copyist. Die-cutters, screw presses and paper exist; type metal and oily ink are unsolved. Local: goldsmiths and die-cutters of the Zecca; cartolai and copyists; paper from Fabriano. Elsewhere: Korea, cast metal type in use; China, wooden movable type (Wang Zhen, c. 1298) beside woodblocks.
- **Reproducing images (woodcut, engraving, etching, lithography)** [`lithography_engraving`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lithography_engraving.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept high. Goldsmiths engrave silver and fill the lines with niello; nobody takes an impression on paper. Pictures are multiplied only by copying. Local: goldsmiths (niello work). Elsewhere: China, woodcut book illustrations.
- **Relay post and public mail** [`postal_system`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/postal_system.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Merchant companies and the commune send their own couriers; Avignon is two weeks away. The failed companies' networks are gone. Nothing is open to the public at a fixed price. Local: couriers of the merchant companies and the Mercanzia; messengers of the Signoria. Elsewhere: Avignon, papal couriers; Mongol lands, relay stations described by Marco Polo; Mamluk Egypt, horse relays and pigeon post.
- **Newspapers and periodicals** [`newspapers_periodicals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/newspapers_periodicals.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. News comes in merchants' letters, read aloud and copied, and from criers and pulpits. A regular copied news sheet would be new; the priors would want to control it. Local: merchant company correspondence; banditori (town criers).
- **Scientific journal and peer review** [`scientific_journal`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_journal.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Scholars exchange Latin letters and disputed questions. Without printing, a periodical means paying copyists for every issue.
- **Encyclopedias and dictionaries** [`encyclopedia_reference_works`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/encyclopedia_reference_works.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Isidore, Vincent of Beauvais and Bartholomew the Englishman are the reference works; Brunetto Latini's Tesoro circulates in Tuscan. All are unverified, hand-copied and silent on workshop practice. Local: Brunetto Latini's Tesoro; convent libraries of Santa Maria Novella and Santa Croce.
- **Library catalogue and classification** [`library_catalogue`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/library_catalogue.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Convent libraries keep inventories by desk, with reference books chained. Author indexes and a mark for each volume are rare. Local: libraries of Santa Croce, Santa Maria Novella and Santo Spirito. Elsewhere: Paris, Sorbonne library catalogue (1338); Avignon, papal library inventories.
- **Pencil, steel pen and durable ink** [`pencil_steel_pen`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pencil_steel_pen.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept high. Everyone writes with quill and iron-gall ink and takes notes on wax tablets. Painters draw with lead or silver stylus and charcoal. Graphite is unknown. Local: painters' workshops; goldsmiths (could cut metal nibs).
- **Shorthand (stenography)** [`shorthand`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/shorthand.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept high. Notaries write heavily abbreviated Latin. Listeners take down sermons from hurried notes and memory. Roman shorthand signs are a rumour from old monastic books. Local: Arte dei Giudici e Notai (about 600 notaries by Villani's count).
- **Typewriter** [`typewriter`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/typewriter.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Copying documents (copying press, carbon paper, stencil duplicator)** [`copying_duplicating`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copying_duplicating.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Every letter is copied by hand into a copy-book, and every statute by a paid scribe. Lampblack, wax, oil and thin paper exist. Local: merchant companies; chancery of the Signoria.
- **Braille (tactile writing for blind people)** [`braille_tactile_writing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/braille_tactile_writing.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. The blind live as beggars, singers or musicians and learn by ear. Local: Francesco Landini, a young Florentine blind from childhood smallpox, later the city's great organist.
- **Sign languages of deaf people** [`sign_languages`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sign_languages.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. People born deaf are held unteachable and limited in law. Monks use sign lists during hours of silence.
- **Knowledge in the vernacular; translation movements** [`vernacular_translation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/vernacular_translation.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Tuscan is a written language of poetry, chronicles, sermons, account books and translated classics. Medicine, law, theology and university teaching stay Latin. Greek is unread. Local: Dante's Commedia (read and glossed); Giovanni Villani's chronicle; abacus-school textbooks; Tuscan versions of Vegetius, Livy and the Sphere.
- **Beacons, flag codes and heliograph** [`signal_beacons_flag_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/signal_beacons_flag_codes.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Castles and watchtowers pass agreed alarms by fire, smoke and bells; the city's bells call citizens to arms. No code for arbitrary messages.
- **Optical telegraph (semaphore network)** [`optical_telegraph`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/optical_telegraph.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept high. Signal fires exist for war. A coded line of towers would give the Signoria faster news of armies and grain ships; without telescopes the stations must stand close.
- **Standard time and time zones** [`standard_time_zones`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standard_time_zones.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Hours are rung by church bells from sundials and custom, and counted from sunset. Florence has no public mechanical clock yet. Nobody needs two towns to agree.
